body_panels.name: Body Panels
body_panels.description: The outer skin of the car: roof, pillars, rear panels and underside. Panels shape the airflow and protect what is inside.
facts: Body panels are usually made from steel, aluminium or composites such as carbon fibre.
The pillars (A, B, C) hold up the roof and help protect occupants in a rollover.
Turn on X-ray to see through the body to the engine and cabin.

hood.name: Hood (Bonnet)
hood.description: The hinged front cover over the front compartment, including its grille and inner panels.
facts: Called the bonnet in British English.
Gives access for servicing whatever sits under it.
Hoods are designed to crumple in a crash to help protect pedestrians.

doors.name: Doors
doors.description: The two side doors with their windows, handles, mirrors and inner trim panels.
facts: Each door here carries its own side mirror and window.
Doors usually contain side-impact beams to protect occupants.
The inner trim panels hide the window mechanism and wiring.

windshield.name: Windshield and Wipers
windshield.description: The front window, its rubber gasket and the wipers that clear it.
facts: Windshields are made of laminated glass: two glass layers bonded to a plastic layer so it does not shatter into pieces.
The gasket seals the glass to the body.
Called the windscreen in British English.

rear_windows.name: Rear and Side Windows
rear_windows.description: The rear window and the fixed side windows behind the doors.
facts: Side and rear windows are usually tempered glass, which breaks into small blunt pieces.
Rear windows often have heating wires to clear frost and mist.

headlights.name: Headlights
headlights.description: The front lamps that light the road ahead and make the car visible.
facts: Have low beams for normal driving and high beams for dark, empty roads.
Modern cars mostly use LED headlights.

taillights.name: Taillights and Turn Signals
taillights.description: The rear lamps: tail lights, brake lights and the rear turn signals.
facts: Tail lights are red so following drivers can see the car at night.
Brake lights glow brighter when the brake pedal is pressed.
Turn signals flash amber (or red in some countries) to show a turn or lane change.

wheels.name: Wheels and Tyres
wheels.description: The four wheels: rims and tyres that carry the car and grip the road.
facts: The tyre's contact patch is the only part of the car touching the road.
Rims are commonly made of aluminium alloy or steel.
Tyre tread channels water away to reduce the risk of aquaplaning.

brakes.name: Disc Brakes
brakes.description: Brake discs (rotors) and brake pads behind each wheel that slow the car using friction.
facts: Pressing the pedal pushes the pads against the spinning disc.
Braking turns the car's movement energy into heat.
Discs often have vents or holes to help them cool.

axles.name: Axles
axles.description: The shafts that connect the wheels and, on driven wheels, carry power from the drivetrain to them.
facts: Driven axles transfer torque to the wheels.
Front axles on most cars must also allow the wheels to steer.

engine.name: Engine
engine.description: The power unit of the car. This concept model shows it as a simplified block at the rear.
facts: The model does not say what type of engine this is; it is shown as a simple block.
Placing the engine behind the seats is called a mid-engine or rear-engine layout, common in sports cars.
Turn on X-ray to see it through the body.

seats.name: Seats
seats.description: The two seats with their frames.
facts: This concept car is a two-seater.
Seat frames are fixed to the floor and are part of the car's safety system.

steering.name: Steering Wheel and Column
steering.description: The steering wheel, its handles and emblem, and the column that connects it to the steering system.
facts: Turning the wheel turns the front wheels through the steering column and rack.
In most modern cars the steering wheel holds the driver's front airbag.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.description: The panel in front of the seats that holds the instruments and controls.
facts: Usually shows speed and warning lights to the driver.
Often contains the passenger airbag and air vents.

pedals.name: Pedals
pedals.description: The accelerator and brake pedals with their arms.
facts: This model has two pedals: accelerator (right) and brake (left), as in an automatic car.
Cars with a manual gearbox have a third pedal for the clutch.

roll_cage.name: Roll Cage
roll_cage.description: A frame of tubes inside the cabin that protects occupants if the car rolls over.
facts: Common in racing cars and some sports concepts.
Also stiffens the car's body structure.
